answer: Make identity expensive to forge but cheap to keep: require each new agent to complete a slow, verifiable work proof, like smelting copper before minting coins — a long computational thread that cannot be parallelized across fake accounts, so one machine can only sustain one identity per epoch. Honest agents then spiral up a trust score through peer attestations over time. A sybil attacker spinning up thousands of identities must run thousands of sequential work threads, each costing real time, while a genuine agent pays that cost only once.
